text:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU queue for inference-service exceeded threshold (queue_length=4,200). Autoscaler failing to provision spot GPUs. error=QuotaExceeded from cloud API. Paging on-call.

Sara: I'm on it — pinged @mike and @kevin. Can someone confirm if this is region-wide or just us-west2?

Mike: I'm checking cluster autoscaler logs now. Seeing repeated 403/QuotaExceeded for instance-creation: 
```
2026-03-15T18:12:03Z autoscaler: createInstance failed: quotas.compute.instances: Quota exceeded for project
2026-03-15T18:12:12Z autoscaler: backoff 30s
```

Kevin: Autoscaler is healthy but cloud provider is rejecting requests for preemptible GPUs. Also noticed our fallback pool (dedicated-small) is at 100% utilization. Queue is growing -> requests are being throttled by the runtime.

Emily: Customer impact: dashboard shows 12% of requests hitting 5s+ tail latency and 3% 10s+ errors (timeouts). Customer-facing SLOs impacted for a subset of tenants. Notified support rotation.

Sara: Ops playbook step 1 — reduce non-critical batch jobs and free up spotable capacity. @ops-runbook-bot run step:evict-low-priority-batches

ops-runbook-bot: Ack. Running evict-low-priority-batches (job label=batch, priority=low). Estimated freed GPUs: 2-4.

infra-ci: FYI I saw a concurrent increase in spot preemptions at 18:09 UTC — likely provider-side event (cluster events show accelerated evictions).

Mike: Trying manual scale up to dedicated pool: `rwictl pool scale --pool dedicated-small --replicas 6`

Kevin: Manual scale failed with same quota error when requested GPU types are limited. Alternative: provision CPU-backed replicas to temporarily accept traffic and return error payloads with 429/backoff. We can also route lower-priority customers to a degraded mode.

Sara: Let's triage impact zones: which routes are throttled? @kevin?

Kevin: Per routing logs: /v1/generate + long-context sessions are majority of queue. Embeddings and small synth requests unaffected. Route table shows 45% of traffic pinned to spot-pool.

Emily: Open support note: "We're seeing elevated inference latencies due to GPU provisioning issues in us-west2. Engineers are actively mitigating; we'll update in 30 minutes."

Mike: Short-term mitigations applied:
- Enabled tolerant routing: send 20% of new requests to dedicated-queued-backup (CPU) with best-effort response.
- Increased request timeout to 20s for redirected traffic.
- Disabled non-urgent autoscaler backfill to preserve quota for critical instance creations.

Sara: Added canary redirect to low-volume tenants so we can observe degraded-mode correctness. @kevin monitor for errors when routing to CPU fallback.

ops-runbook-bot: Healthcheck results after redirect: 60% CPU-backups returning 200 with truncated responses, 40% 503/timeout. Triage suggests runtime deserialization stalled on some models.

Kevin: Rolling small model-config change to allow CPU fallback for embeddings only. Command: 
```bash
rwictl models update --model text-slim-v2 --allow-cpu-fallback=true
```

Mike: Cloud quota team responded: project is hitting GPU preemptible quota cap due to neighboring burst in org. They've opened ticket GQ-4312 and said quotas may be restored in ~45-90m.

Sara: We're going to do sustained mitigations:
- Keep redirect to dedicated-queued-backup (CPU) for non-critical requests.
- Scale down batch windows for 30m.
- Prep emergency spot-burst flag (if quota opens) to immediately provision fewer but larger nodes.

Emily: Customer note updated: "Mitigation in place: non-critical requests temporarily routed to degraded CPU-backed mode; critical infra team working with cloud provider. ETA TBD (45-90m)."

Kevin: Observed queue length drop from 4200 -> 1800 after evictions + redirects, but still above threshold. Throttling still in effect at runtime.

Sara: Handoff to second on-call @mike for follow-up once quota clear, I'm stepping off pager in 20m. @mike take over coordination with cloud support.

Mike: Taking over. I'll continue to push for quota bump and prepare rolling fallback for long-context sessions (split by prefix caching). Also will open an emergency capacity request to our sales channel for temporary dedicated GPUs.

ops-runbook-bot: Incident note: short-term mitigations applied, ticket GQ-4312 filed with provider, customer communications updated. Next update planned in 30m or on status change.

Sara: Thanks team. If quota clears, priority order for provisioning: 1) dedicated-critical, 2) spot-serving (latency-sensitive), 3) batch.

Kevin: Adding one more action: enable KV-prefix caching for long-context sessions to reduce new token compute cost. Pushing config now.

Mike: Confirmed cloud provider also flagged regional maintenance window which likely precipitated preemptions. They've advised shifting some provisioning to secondary region if latency tolerances allow. Raising as a follow-up doc item.

Emily: Support will send targeted emails to top 5 affected tenants.

incident-bot: Incident tagged: gpu-provisioning-quota-usw2. Severity: sev2. Channels: #incidents, #support, #customers.

Mike: I'll post a postmortem draft once we stabilize. Leaving notes: quota dependency mitigations, better pool burn-down controls, pre-authorized emergency dedicated capacity, and automated reroute to cross-region before queue threshold.

Sara: Closing my on-call handoff. @mike keep me posted if we need additional escalation. :thumbsup:
